_comment_geometry: Nodes 5 and 8 sit high deliberately. Everything else is near ground level, so without them VDOP is roughly 25 and altitude is unrecoverable. Move them back to 8 m in this file and watch the vertical error in the console triple -- that is the coplanarity tax, and it is geometry, not software.

radio._comment_cyclo: Cyclic-prefix detector: keeps a burst the energy gate missed when the lag-N_u autocorrelation says OFDM is present (several dB of margin), and classifies it (uas_ofdm + n_useful/n_cp in the event's hw block). Doppler- and CFO-immune by construction.

sim._comment_carrier: Model the carrier: Doppler from emitter motion plus LO rate offset from the clock discipline. The orbit's ~31 m/s is ~250-400 Hz differential at 2.437 GHz -- enough to null a 10 ms cross-correlation unless the correlator searches Doppler (solver.caf). false restores the old baseband-only sim.
sim._comment_waveform: ofdm = CP-OFDM burst (OcuSync-shaped: QPSK data, fixed pilots, CP 16/128). Gives GCC-HT and the cyclostationary detector real structure. noise = the old flat Gaussian burst, the cleaner choice when isolating solver behaviour.
sim._comment_interference: Per-node local interferer (each node's own Wi-Fi neighbour, distinct centre per node -- NOT a common illuminator, which is the case GCC weighting cannot fix). Off by default so the documented baseline stays clean; set enabled true and toggle GCC-HT in the console to watch the weighting earn its keep.
sim._comment_clock: clock_discipline: gpsdo | holdover | free. gpsdo is a control loop, so error is BOUNDED jitter about UTC (Ornstein-Uhlenbeck, sigma=pps_jitter_s) -- what real GPSDO hardware does. holdover free-runs from the error held when lock was lost. free never disciplines at all and ramps without bound (0.02 ppm = 24 us in 20 min), which is what exposed the correlation-window bug. Switchable live from the console.
sim._comment_multipath: Per-node reflection taps, drawn ONCE per node and reused -- reflectors are fixed geometry, so the bias is static and does not average away. Off by default; the documented baseline assumes free space. Turning it on at 2 MHz costs ~4.6 m horizontal and ~114 m vertical and cannot be fixed by peak-picking: at c/B = 150 m the echoes are unresolvable. Bandwidth is the defence -- 18 MHz brings it to 0.26 m / 35 m.

solver._comment_caf: Cross-ambiguity: correlate over lag AND differential Doppler, then derotate before the precise lag estimate. Needed the moment the carrier is modelled (sim.carrier) or on any real moving emitter; caf_vmax_mps bounds the Doppler search span, scaled by the event's fc.
solver._comment_all_pairs: Correlate every node pair and solve GLS with the full covariance (pair_covariance), instead of everyone-vs-reference with diagonal weights that treat the shared reference's noise as independent per row. ~3.5x the correlation work for 7 nodes.
solver._comment_tight: A burst with 1-2 surviving pairs cannot produce a fix but still constrains an existing track: feed its TDOA rows to the EKF directly, innovation-gated. Recovers the bursts the starved counter used to discard.
solver._comment_gcc: Hannan-Thomson GCC weighting from per-node Welch PSDs, applied on the cached-spectra fast path. ht | none. Needs a structured waveform (sim.waveform ofdm) to do anything; the win case is per-node interference, whose bins carry no cross-channel signal and get crushed.
solver._comment_robust: quality_gate drops a correlation whose peak does not stand out from the noise floor -- a LOST peak is wrong by microseconds and timing_sigma() cannot express that, so it hands garbage nearly full weight. robust applies Huber IRLS so an outlier that still gets through cannot dominate. Both are live-switchable from the console.

_comment_profile: 10-node fleet scanning the 2.4 GHz ISM band. Derived from site.json; the only difference is the dwell block.

dwell._comment: Coordinated scan. Every node derives the dwell index from UTC and takes plan[idx % len(plan)], so ten independently started nodes are on the same channel in the same window without exchanging a message -- which is the whole point, because TDOA correlates IQ BETWEEN nodes and a fleet that disagrees about frequency produces no usable pair at all, not a degraded one. The supernode broadcasts the plan on dc/{site}/dwell so it can be changed at runtime; losing that message costs nothing. Revisit time is dwell_s * len(plan) -- 2 s here. A video downlink is essentially continuous so it is caught every revisit; a sparse control link needs either a shorter plan or channelization.
dwell._comment_rate: Every channel in the plan uses the SAME fs_sps as radio.fs_sps, and must: the node derives n_samples once at construction, so a per-dwell rate change is not applied. Retuning between dwells is cheap; re-rating is not -- on real hardware it re-settles filters and the LO, and it would change the snippet length the correlator assumes. Scan by frequency, not by rate.
dwell._comment_period: dwell_s must NOT be commensurate with the transmit cadence. Measured share across four channels at 2 bursts/s: 0.2 s and 0.3/0.4/0.5 s give an even 25 percent each; 0.35 s gives 28/22/28/21; 0.15 s gives 33/17/34/16; and 0.25 s is degenerate -- only TWO of the four channels are ever sampled, 50/50, because floor(t/0.25) at t=k/2 only ever lands on even indices. The fleet scans diligently and never looks at half the band. Faster is not worse and slower is not safer: check the share.

_comment_cost: 20 Msps x 10 emulated nodes is ~200k samples per node per burst, about 8x config/site.json. This profile demonstrates the coordinator; it is not a laptop profile. Use config/site.json to watch the solver.
